interventions.body: Postoperative prognosis depends on the preoperative PSA and the prostatectomy findings. Extraprostatic extension is documented. Positive surgical margins is documented. Seminal vesicle invasion is documented. Lymphovascular invasion is reported absent. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are needed to refine this prognosis; a future recurrence date cannot be established from surgical risk factors alone. The fixed estimated horizon is 29.84 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 23.87–35.81 months; its coverage has not been validated.

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology reveals several adverse features. The surgical pathology report documents "Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3), pathological stage pT4b. Extraprostatic extension was present; surgical margins were positive; the seminal vesicles were invaded; lymph node metastasis was present." These findings suggest a high-risk disease profile. Countervailing findings include the absence of lymphovascular invasion, which is noted as "absent." The biopsy report identified a Gleason 4+4 pattern. The presence of lymph node metastasis is a significant adverse factor. Missing postoperative PSA data prevents assessment of biochemical recurrence. The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding the extent of disease. Postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory are crucial information that would revise the prognosis.

nodal_contradiction: The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding the extent of disease

attempts.text: The postoperative pathology revealed a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) diagnosis with pathological stage pT4b. Adverse findings included positive surgical margins, invasion of the seminal vesicles, and the presence of lymph node metastasis. The biopsy identified a Gleason 4+4 (ISUP grade group 4) pattern. The presence of lymph node metastasis is an adverse finding. Countervailing findings include the absence of lymphovascular invasion, as noted in the surgical pathology report: "lymphovascular invasion was absent." The pNx status does not establish node-negative disease, and missing nodal sampling widens uncertainty regarding the extent of disease. Postoperative PSA is not recorded, so biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would revise the prognosis.
